annotation.title_clean: Trustworthy AI in Aotearoa New Zealand: AI Principles
annotation.title_en: Trustworthy AI in Aotearoa New Zealand: AI Principles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: AI Forum New Zealand, Law, Society and Ethics Working Group
annotation.summary_en: AI Forum New Zealand's March 2020 voluntary principles for trustworthy AI: fairness and justice; reliability, security and privacy; transparency; human oversight and accountability; and wellbeing. It stresses that existing law still applies, that human rights and Te Tiriti o Waitangi matter, and that self-regulation does not replace government regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Five principles: fairness and justice; reliability, security and privacy; transparency; human oversight and accountability; wellbeing
Existing laws on consumer protection, privacy, liability, IP and human rights apply to AI
Harm-capable technologies should not be deployed until accountability and liability are determined
Respect for Māori rights under Te Tiriti o Waitangi
Self-regulation is no substitute for democratically mandated, enforceable rules
